style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: A king's psalm assembled from David's older songs -- lines of Psalm 18 and Psalm 8 reworked into a prayer for a nation's peace. It opens as a soldier's blessing: blessed be the LORD my Rock, who trains my hands for war -- my covenant love, my fortress, my tower, my deliverer, my shield. Then, without warning, the question of Psalm 8 in a minor key: LORD, what is man, that You take notice of him? Man is like a breath; his days a passing shadow. The answer is the theophany of Psalm 18 asked for again: bend Your heavens and come down, touch the mountains so they smoke, flash lightning, shoot arrows, reach down from above and pull me out of deep water, out of the hands of foreigners whose mouths speak emptiness and whose right hand swears lies. A new song follows -- to the God who gives victory to kings and rescues His servant David from the deadly sword. And then the psalm turns from battle to the reason for it, the most domestic vision in the Psalter: sons like well-grown plants, daughters like carved corner-pillars of a palace, barns full, flocks in the thousands, oxen strong, no breach in the wall, no exile, no cry of distress in the streets. Happy the people who have it so; happy the people whose God is the LORD. War is for the sake of the farm.

1.text: Of David. Blessed be the LORD, my Rock, who trains my hands for the fight and my fingers for war --
1.amp: A Psalm of David. Blessed [barak] be the LORD [YHWH] my strength ['my rock', tsur, the KJV margin], which teaches [lamad] my hands [yad] to war [qerab -- the close fight], and my fingers [etsba] to fight [milchamah -- battle]:
1.notes: barukh YHWH tsuri (H1288, H3068, H6697): the Rock of Psalm 18:2 -- ha-melammed yadai la-qerab, etsbeotai la-milchamah (H3925, H3027, H7128, H676, H4421): Psalm 18:34's line, with a second clause: fingers for battle -- the bowman's fingers, the sling's. Skill in war credited to a Teacher.

2.text: my covenant love and my fortress, my high tower and my deliverer, my shield, the One I take refuge in, who subdues my people under me.
2.amp: My goodness ['my mercy', chesed -- my covenant love, the KJV margin], and my fortress [metsudah]; my high tower [misgab], and my deliverer [palat]; my shield [magen], and He in whom I trust [chasah -- take refuge]; who subdues [radad -- beats down, spreads under] my people [am] under me.
2.notes: chasdi u-metsudati (H2617, H4686): 'my chesed' -- God Himself called my covenant love, one of the few places in the Psalter (with Psalm 59:10, 17) He is named by the attribute -- misgabbi u-mephalti li (H4869, H6403), maginni u-bo chasiti (H4043, H2620): the titles of Psalm 18:2 again. ha-roded ammi tachtai (H7286, H5971): who spreads my people under me -- a king's rule as God's gift, not his grip.

3.text: O LORD, what is man, that You take notice of him? What is the son of a mortal, that You give him a thought?
3.amp: LORD [YHWH], what is man [adam], that You take knowledge [yada] of him! or the son [ben] of man [enosh -- frail mortal], that You make account [chashab -- reckon, think of] of him!
3.notes: YHWH mah-adam va-tedaehu (H120, H3045): Psalm 8:4's question in a warrior's mouth -- ben-enosh va-techashvehu (H1121, H582, H2803): the son of enosh, frail man, that You reckon with him at all. After the armory of verses 1-2, the psalmist looks at himself and cannot see why God bothers.

4.text: Man is like a breath; his days are like a shadow passing by.
4.amp: Man [adam] is like [damah] to vanity [hebel -- a breath, vapor]: his days [yom] are as a shadow [tsel] that passes away [abar].
4.notes: adam la-hebel damah (H120, H1892, H1819): man RESEMBLES a breath -- Ecclesiastes' hebel -- yamav ke-tsel over (H3117, H6738, H5674): his days a passing shadow, Psalm 102:11's image. The king who trains for war admits he is vapor; the admission is why he prays instead of only fighting.

5.text: O LORD, bend Your heavens and come down; touch the mountains, and they will smoke.
5.amp: Bow [natah -- bend] Your heavens [shamayim], O LORD [YHWH], and come down [yarad]: touch [naga] the mountains [har], and they shall smoke [ashan].
5.notes: YHWH hat-shamekha ve-tered (H5186, H8064, H3381): Psalm 18:9's theophany, no longer remembered but REQUESTED -- do it again. ga be-harim ve-yeeshanu (H5060, H2022, H6225): touch the mountains and they smoke, Sinai's smoke (cf. Exodus 19:18; Psalm 104:32). A finger on a mountain, and the mountain burns.

6.text: Flash out lightning and scatter them; shoot Your arrows and throw them into confusion.
6.amp: Cast forth [baraq -- flash] lightning [baraq], and scatter [puts] them: shoot out [shalach] Your arrows [chets], and destroy [hamam -- rout, throw into panic] them.
6.notes: beroq baraq u-tephitsem (H1299, H1300, H6327): flash the flash -- the verb and the noun are the same word -- and scatter them; shelach chitsekha u-tehummem (H7971, H2671, H2000): arrows sent, enemies routed in panic by hamam, Psalm 18:14 word for word, in the imperative.

7.text: Stretch out Your hands from on high; snatch me away and deliver me out of the great waters, from the hand of the sons of foreign lands,
7.amp: Send [shalach] Your hand ['hands', yad, the KJV margin] from above [marom]; rid [patsah -- snatch away, set free] me, and deliver [natsal] me out of great [rav] waters [mayim], from the hand [yad] of strange [nekar -- foreign] children [ben];
7.notes: shelach yadekha mi-marom (H7971, H3027, H4791): Psalm 18:16's reaching hand -- petseni ve-hatsileni mi-mayim rabbim (H6475, H5337, H4325, H7227), out of the many waters -- mi-yad bene nekar (H1121, H5236): from the hand of foreigners' sons. The rescue David remembered in Psalm 18 is the rescue he needs again.

8.text: whose mouths speak emptiness, and whose right hand is a right hand raised in falsehood.
8.amp: Whose mouth [peh] speaks [dabar] vanity [shav -- emptiness, falsehood], and their right hand [yamin] is a right hand of falsehood [sheqer -- lies].
8.notes: asher pihem dibber-shav (H6310, H1696, H7723): mouths that speak shav, the empty word of the third commandment -- vi-minam yemin shaqer (H3225, H8267): and their right hand -- the hand raised to swear an oath -- is a hand of lies. Treaties with such men are worthless; only God's hand (v. 7) can be trusted.

9.text: O God, I will sing a new song to You; on a ten-stringed lute I will make music to You --
9.amp: I will sing [shir] a new [chadash] song [shir] unto You, O God [Elohim]: upon a psaltery [nebel -- lute] and an instrument of ten strings [asor] will I sing praises [zamar] unto You.
9.notes: Elohim shir chadash ashirah lakh (H430, H7892, H2319, H7891): the new song of Psalms 96 and 98 -- be-nebel asor azammerah-lakh (H5035, H6218, H2167): on the ten-stringed lute, Psalm 92:3's instrument. Before the rescue arrives, the song is already promised.

10.text: to the One who gives victory to kings, who snatches David His servant away from the deadly sword.
10.amp: It is He that gives [natan] salvation ['victory', teshuah, the KJV margin] unto kings [melek]: who delivers [patsah -- snatches away] David His servant [ebed] from the hurtful [ra -- evil, deadly] sword [chereb].
10.notes: ha-noten teshuah la-melakhim (H5414, H8668, H4428): the giver of victory to KINGS -- plural; every crown's success is on loan -- ha-potseh et-David abdo me-chereb raah (H6475, H1732, H5650, H2719, H7451): who snatches David His servant from the evil sword. David names himself in the third person, as a servant reporting on his Master.

11.text: Snatch me away and deliver me from the hand of the sons of foreign lands, whose mouths speak emptiness, and whose right hand is a right hand raised in falsehood --
11.amp: Rid [patsah] me, and deliver [natsal] me from the hand [yad] of strange [nekar] children [ben], whose mouth [peh] speaks [dabar] vanity [shav], and their right hand [yamin] is a right hand of falsehood [sheqer]:
11.notes: Verses 7-8 repeated as a refrain (H6475, H5337, H3027, H5236, H1121, H6310, H1696, H7723, H3225, H8267) -- the plea said twice, framing the new song. The repetition is the psalm's hinge: after it, the subject changes from war to what the war is for.

12.text: so that our sons may be like plants grown tall in their youth, and our daughters like corner pillars, carved in the style of a palace;
12.amp: That our sons [ben] may be as plants [neti -- saplings] grown up [gadal] in their youth [neurim]; that our daughters [bath] may be as corner stones [zavith -- corner pillars], polished ['cut', chatab -- hewn, the KJV margin] after the similitude [tabnith -- pattern] of a palace [hekal];
12.notes: asher banenu ki-netiim megudalim bi-neurehem (H1121, H5195, H1431, H5271): sons like saplings grown big while still young -- benotenu khe-zaviyyot mechuttavot tabnit hekal (H1323, H2106, H2404, H8403, H1964): daughters like the carved corner-pillars of a palace -- load-bearing and beautiful at once. The war of verses 1-11 was for these: a generation allowed to grow.

13.text: so that our storehouses may be full, supplying every kind of provision; our flocks bearing thousands and tens of thousands in our fields;
13.amp: That our garners [mazu -- storehouses] may be full [male], affording [puq -- yielding] all manner of store ['from kind to kind', zan -- kind, sort, the KJV margin]: that our sheep [tson] may bring forth thousands [alaph] and ten thousands [rabab] in our streets [chuts -- open fields];
13.notes: mezavenu meleim mephiqim mi-zan el-zan (H4200, H4392, H6329, H2177): barns full, yielding from kind to kind -- every sort of provision -- tsonenu maaliphot merubbabot be-chutsotenu (H6629, H503, H7231, H2351): flocks THOUSANDING and ten-thousanding -- the Hebrew makes verbs of the numbers -- in the open country. Deuteronomy 28's blessing on a farm.

14.text: our oxen heavy with loads; no breach in the walls, no going out into captivity, no cry of distress in our streets.
14.amp: That our oxen [alluph -- the tame cattle] may be strong to labour ['able to bear burdens, or, loaden with flesh', sabal, the KJV margin]; that there be no breaking in [perets -- breach], nor going out [yatsa]; that there be no complaining [tsevachah -- outcry] in our streets [rechob -- open squares].
14.notes: alluphenu mesubbalim (H441, H5445): oxen bearing loads -- or, the margin, loaded with flesh: fat and strong. en-perets ve-en yotset (H6556, H3318): no breach in the wall, no going out -- no exile -- ve-en tsevachah bi-rechovotenu (H6682, H7339): no outcry in the squares. Peace defined by three absences: no raiders, no deportation, no screaming.

15.text: Oh the blessedness of the people for whom it is so! Oh the blessedness of the people whose God is the LORD!
15.amp: Happy [esher -- blessed] is that people [am], that is in such a case [kakah -- thus]: yea, happy is that people, whose God [Elohim] is the LORD [YHWH].
15.notes: ashre ha-am she-kakhah lo (H835, H5971, H3602): blessed the people for whom it is THUS -- the farm, the children, the quiet streets -- ashre ha-am she-YHWH Elohav (H3068, H430): and then the correction that keeps the first line from being mere prosperity: blessed the people whose God is the LORD. The second beatitude is the cause of the first; the psalm ends on the Name.
